string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of its four direct-administered municipalities. It is the country\'s political, cultural and international exchange centre, home to the central government and many national institutions. With an area of about 16,400 square kilometres and a permanent population of roughly 21.8 million, it is one of the most populous cities in the world. The city blends a long imperial history with rapid modern development: landmarks such as the Forbidden City, the Great Wall and the Temple of Heaven attract millions of visitors every year, while its economy, technology sector and universities continue to grow.

Shanghai is a global city located at the mouth of the Yangtze River on China\'s eastern coast. It is one of the four direct-administered municipalities and the country\'s leading financial, commercial and shipping centre. Covering about 6,300 square kilometres and home to nearly 25 million people, it is one of the largest cities in the world. The city is famous for its modern skyline along the Huangpu River, including the Oriental Pearl Tower, and for historic landmarks such as the Bund. As an international hub, Shanghai hosts major stock exchanges, multinational companies and one of the busiest container ports, and it continues to drive innovation and economic growth across the Yangtze River Delta.

Chongqing is a major city in southwestern China and the largest direct-administered municipality by both area and population. Covering roughly 82,000 square kilometres, it is home to more than 30 million permanent residents, making it one of the biggest cities in the world. The city is built among mountains and rivers: the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet in its centre, and it is famous for its steep hills, dense bridges, dramatic night views and spicy Sichuan-style cuisine. As a key transport, manufacturing and logistics hub in western China, Chongqing has grown rapidly into a modern economic centre, even though much of its territory still consists of rural counties and deep valleys.

Tianjin is one of China\'s four direct-administered municipalities and the largest coastal city in northern China. Located about 120 kilometres from Beijing on the Bohai Sea, it has long served as the main port and gateway for the capital region. The municipality covers more than 11,000 square kilometres and is home to roughly 14 million people. Tianjin is an important centre for advanced manufacturing, international shipping and financial innovation, and it was among the first Chinese cities opened to foreign trade. The city preserves a distinctive blend of Chinese and European architecture from its treaty-port history alongside modern harbour facilities, making it a key economic hub of the Bohai Rim region.
